title: Second premise: Saints know needs, pray with greater charity, and are mediators of intercession not redemption
source_text: XLV. Secundo supponunt Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae Sanctos in coelis non solum viventium necessitates nosse; sed majori, quam dum in terris agerent, charitate Deum pro illorum salute deprecari. Neque tantum illos in communi pro Ecclesia militante orare; sed etiam in particulari pro necessitatibus singulorum, qui ad illorum opem, & patrocinium confugiunt. Ac proinde Sanctos merito dici posse intercessores nostros, & Advocatos apud Deum & Mediatores, non quidem Redemptionis, quod soli Christo competit, sed intercessionis.
pass_a_gloss: Secondly the Doctors of the Roman Church suppose that the Saints in heaven not only know the necessities of the living, but with greater charity than while they lived on earth deprecate God for their salvation. And that they pray not only in common for the militant Church, but also in particular for the necessities of individuals who flee to their help and patronage. And therefore the Saints can deservedly be called our intercessors, and Advocates before God and Mediators—not indeed of Redemption, which belongs to Christ alone, but of intercession.
pass_b_english: Roman premise two: heaven knows living needs and prays with greater charity than on earth.
They plead both for the Church militant and for individuals who seek their patronage.
Called intercessors and advocates—mediators of intercession, never of redemption.

choices.english: not of Redemption … but of intercession
choices.why: Core Roman distinction reserving redemption to Christ.
